Colombia–European Union Free Trade Agreement (in force 2013)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 2155 of 2021 (Social Investment Act) amending Tax Statute Article 631-8; DIAN Resolution 000164 of 2021 establishing the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUB); Law 526 of 1999; Law 1121 of 2006; Decree 830 of 2021; and Decree 1068 of 2015 (AML/CFT regime supervised by UIAF).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry or Companies House/CI in shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, if non-Hague signatory, Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing a Colombian legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in domicile of each officer/resident agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy of each ultimate beneficial owner and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (notarized copy)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for each direct shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (for foreign banks)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all shareholders, directors, officers and ultimate beneficial owners against Colombian UIAF lists, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and domestic Colombian terrorist-financing and money-laundering registries. Enhanced due diligence required for any Politically Exposed Person (PEP), foreign or domestic, and for any direct or indirect ownership sourced from OFAC-sanctioned jurisdictions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Confecámaras - Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) online name clearance module and local Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must appear in Spanish or use adapted Spanish transliteration of foreign words; must include the abbreviation 'S.A.S.' or 'SAS' as the corporate form suffix; only letters, numbers, and common commercial symbols are allowed; no confusion with existing registered names or trademarks.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If name clearance is rejected, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request within 10 business days to the issuing Chamber of Commerce, citing the specific grounds of confusion or non-compliance, and may invoke the administrative appeal remedies under Law 1437 of 2011 (CPACA). Upon renewed rejection, the applicant may use the name as proposed after a 30-day cooling-off period or request judicial review through the contentious-administrative jurisdiction.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this industry (agri-commodity brokerage) only if the virtual office provider allows postal service receipt, legal process service, and official communications; however, DIAN and the Chamber of Commerce reserve the right to require a local physical presence for tax inspection and commercial record access. A physical registered office is strongly recommended to avoid administrative friction.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantifiable risk for the proposed activity; estimated at 15% annually due to standard anti-fraud controls by Cámara de Comercio and DIAN, with no industry-specific enforcement targeting.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarized public deed of incorporation (Escritura Pública) for S.A.S.
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notary tariff schedule of the Superintendencia de Notariado y Registro, based on capital declared

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and translation package for foreign shareholder documentation (passports, powers of attorney, incumbency certificates)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Colombian state apostille fee plus certified translator per-page tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: DIAN administrative fee for new registrant UBO filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered address provision (virtual office package – standard) for one year

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market standard fixed fee for SAS incorporation package (including dossiers and AML/PEP clearance)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada) as supplemented by articles 352-369 of the Colombian Commercial Code; registration provisions under the Substantive Commercial Code, articles 164-174.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (Chamber of Commerce of the registered office), operating through the Registro Único Empresarial (RUES) and overseen by the Superintendencia de Sociedades.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation instrument) filed with the Chamber of Commerce for mercantile registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a S.A.S.; the subscribed capital may be paid in installments over a maximum of two years, and no escrow or deposit account is required under Colombian law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the Company approves the subscription and payment terms of the founding shares, and authorizes the legal representative to open a corporate bank account and receive all capital contributions; (2) that the registered office of the Company is fixed at [address], municipality of [city], Republic of Colombia; (3) that [Name] is appointed as legal representative, [Name] as secretary, and, if legally required, [Name] as fiscal auditor; (4) that the legal representative is authorized to execute all filings, publications, and registrations before the Chamber of Commerce, DIAN, and any other competent authority; and (5) that all prior acts performed for formation are hereby ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chamber of Commerce through the RUES online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search ('consulta de homonimia') to obtain a certificate of non-confusion with existing Colombian mercantile entities. The request must include the desired corporate name, the proposed main business activity, and the applicant's identification document. The system will issue a 'certificado de homonimia' confirming that the name is available for a specified period.
required_dossiers: Name search application form
Copy of the requesting shareholder's government-issued ID
Basic statement of business purpose
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name shows a previous registration or confusing similarity, file a new name request through the same portal with alternatives; no additional fee beyond the initial tariff if filed within the same business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the incorporation instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (if elected) and the Chamber of Commerce registry office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the private incorporation document containing the articles of incorporation, S.A.S. representations, share subscription list, capital schedule, management structure, and legal address. Execute the document before all founding shareholders or their lawful representatives, with signatures authenticated by a notary if required by the Chamber of Commerce or if the incorporators prefer a public deed.
required_dossiers: Incorporation document (Documento Privado de Constitución) or public deed
Notarized shareholders' identification for signatures
Name availability certificate (homoclinia) within validity period
Power of attorney if a shareholder acts through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or notary raises deficiencies, correct the affected clauses in an addendum or amendment and resubmit; any statutory fee is generally waived for a first corrected submission within the five-day response period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chamber of Commerce and Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed incorporation instrument, together with the required filing forms, to the Chamber of Commerce for registration in the Mercantile Registry. Upon issuance of the chamber registration certificate, complete the RUES data transfer to DIAN to obtain the Número de Identificación Tributaria (NIT) and the Registro Único Tributario (RUT), through the DIAN website or at the nearest DIAN office.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the incorporation instrument
Certificate of absence of homonymy
Documentation of legal representative appointment
RUT pre-registration form through RUES
Proof of the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects or queries the RUT application, resubmit the corrected data online and upload the missing annexes; if the chamber registration is delayed, execute a legal clearance and request the Superintendencia de Sociedades to compel the registry within the statutory term.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chamber of Commerce and, where applicable, the Superintendencia de Sociedades
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the tax registration is complete, legalize the mandatory corporate books: the share subscription and registration book, the minutes book, and the register of shareholders. File the appointment of the legal representative and the initial board resolutions with the Chamber of Commerce to update the Mercantile Registry. Submit any required beneficial ownership information through the RUES system.
required_dossiers: Corporate books (register of shareholders and minutes book)
Certified copy of the board resolution appointing officers
Legal representative's identification and acceptance letter
Beneficial owner declaration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber identifies missing signatures or unsealed book pages, complete and initial the relevant pages within the chamber's prescribed correction period; for the beneficial ownership report, amend the online declaration and resubmit before the penalty deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal commercial registration and fire safety closure
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Secretaría de Hacienda of the municipality and the local fire department (Cuerpo de Bomberos)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the operational office with the municipal business registry (Registro de Establecimiento de Comercio) and request the municipal business tax (ICA) registration from the local treasury. Obtain the fire safety inspection certificate for the commercial premises and ensure compliance with the minimum occupational health and safety obligations for the administrative staff.
required_dossiers: Municipal business registration form
Copy of the RUT with the new business establishment code
Certificate of occupancy for the office
Fire safety inspection certificate
Copy of the lease or property title for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the local registry questions the establishment classification, submit a written clarification supported by the RUT and the company's purpose clause; if fire safety deficiencies are identified, remediate the physical issues and request a re-inspection within the municipality's standard fifteen-day corrective window.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no industrial license required for agricultural commodity brokerage and vessel chartering under ISIC 4631; general commercial supervision is exercised by the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal commercial business registration (Registro de Establecimiento de Comercio) and fire safety certificate; no industry-specific operational license mandated

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not required - brokerage, trading, and chartering activities do not involve physical production, manufacturing, or land alteration, and therefore are outside the categories that require an EIA or environmental registration
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A - no industrial wastewater, VOC emissions, or waste streams are generated by the administrative offices; if future warehousing or physical handling of grains is added, the company must reclassify under the applicable environmental licensing regime.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection certificate for the registered office, municipal occupancy permit, and occupational health and safety (SG-SST) compliance documentation must be maintained at the place of business.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) — Colombia's national tax and customs authority. Principal electronic portal: MUISCA (Modelo Único de Ingresos, Servicios y Control Automatizado) via www.dian.gov.co; export licensing and exporter registration are handled through the Ventanilla Única de Comercio Exterior (VUCE), the interagency foreign-trade single window.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned S.A.S. is incorporated before a local Cámara de Comercio, which automatically triggers tax pre-registration; DIAN then issues the NIT and the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) through MUISCA. The RUT records the statutory NIT, the ISIC 4631 activity code, 'Responsable del IVA – Régimen Común' status, withholding-agent markers, and exporter status. The company must also obtain a DIAN-recognized digital signature for e-invoicing and, for bulk-grain exports, complete its VUCE exporter registration and route export proceeds through an authorized Colombian foreign-exchange intermediary; non-resident shareholders need a NIT only when they become direct taxpayers on Colombian-source transactions or dividends.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the S.A.S. is taxed as a standalone corporate taxpayer under Colombia's territorial-source regime; entity income is not attributed to shareholders, and Colombian-source dividends distributed to non-residents are subject to dividend withholding tax rather than pass-through taxation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia does not operate a US-style check-the-box system and offers no general hybrid-mismatch election. Available statutory options for the S.A.S. include: (i) the optional Régimen Simple de Tributación (RST) for eligible taxpayers with ordinary revenue below approximately 4,500 UVT (COP 211.8 million in 2024), which will normally be unavailable for bulk-commodity trading turnover; (ii) elective consolidated income-tax filing for qualifying economic groups ('Grupo Tributario') subject to DIAN authorization; (iii) advance pricing agreements (APAs) with DIAN to fix transfer-pricing margins for commodity brokerage commissions; and (iv) authorized-exporter status for preferential origin declarations. The simplified VAT regime is not an election for an S.A.S., which is always a common-regime IVA responsible party.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA — Impuesto sobre las Ventas (national value-added tax), supplemented at municipal level by the Impuesto de Industria y Comercio (ICA) and, for selected transactions, the national impuesto al consumo.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For Colombian legal entities there is no de minimis turnover threshold: an S.A.S. engaged in taxable supplies must register for IVA/NIT from its first taxable sale under the Estatuto Tributario and Decree 1625/2016. Non-resident digital-service suppliers must register only when Colombian-source revenue exceeds 30,000 UVT per calendar year (COP 1,411,950,000 in 2024). The former simplified-regime exemption is restricted to natural persons under UVT limits and does not apply to corporations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All IVA-responsible taxpayers must issue electronic invoices (Factura Electrónica de Venta, FEVE) under DIAN Resolution 000012/2021; each export invoice must carry a CUFE code and the issuer's digital signature and be transmitted for validation through the MUISCA platform or an authorized technology provider before delivery to the counterparty. For high-volume and designated taxpayers, DIAN Resolution 000165/2023 mandates real-time pre-clearance ('validación previa') of the XML invoice, cross-checking the seller's RUT, CUFE, commodity description, and — for exports — linkage with the customs export declaration (DEX). Purchases from non-invoicing suppliers are evidenced by an electronic 'documento soporte' (CUDS), and in-country movements of bulk grains require the interoperable electronic transport document (e-remisión).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods qualify for 0% IVA where they physically leave Colombian customs territory as 'exportación definitiva', are sold to a foreign buyer, and are evidenced by a DIAN-accepted Declaración de Exportación (DEX); the exporter then credits and refunds input VAT embedded in commodity purchases, inland freight, stevedoring and vessel costs. Services qualify under Article 481 E.T. where the buyer is non-resident and the service is rendered from Colombia but used or exploited exclusively abroad; ship-brokerage/commission arrangements for international grain voyages must demonstrate that the benefit accrues entirely outside Colombia. Exporters claim the zero rate at the FEVE level and through the bimestral IVA return, retaining charter-party/FOB sales, commission agreements and the export FEVE for each transaction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Declaración de Exportación (DEX) with 'levante' (shipment release) recorded in DIAN's MUISCA system
Transport document — Electronic Bill of Lading or charter-party bill evidencing loading, vessel name and destination
Commercial invoice (factura comercial) in FEVE format with CUFE and digital signature
Packing list (lista de empaque) including bulk-cargo tonnage and commodity grade certifications
Phytosanitary export certificate issued by the Instituto Colombiano Agropecuario (ICA) for soybeans and corn
Certificate of origin (where preferential tariff treatment is claimed under Colombia's trade agreements)

Foreign-exchange settlement certificate (certificado de reintegro / declaración de cambio por exportaciones) issued by an authorized Colombian bank, evidencing repatriation through the documentary credit or SWIFT wire
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN subjects commodity exporters to a targeted export-VAT audit and may require a bank guarantee for refund balances above regulatory thresholds. An overturned zero-rating gives rise to assessment of 19% IVA on the invoice amount, clawback of every refunded input VAT with moratory interest, and a 'sanción por inexactitud' (Article 647 E.T.) generally equal to 100%–200% of the tax understated or the unauthorized refund. Falsified DEX or sham export circuits additionally trigger customs penalties under the Decree 1165/2019 framework, possible 'contrabando' classification, seizure of commodities, suspension of the company's e-invoicing authorization and exporter registration, and criminal liability of managers under tax-fraud and smuggling statutes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (Colombia's independent central bank); foreign exchange administration jointly exercised with the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) as market supervisor and the DIAN as tax/customs authority. Primary legal framework: Law 9 of 1991, Resolution 8 of 2000, and the Banco de la República's Circular Reglamentaria DCIN-83.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso (COP) operates under a free-floating exchange rate regime with a liquid USD/COP market. Current-account operations (goods, services, transport) are freely convertible and must be channeled through authorized foreign exchange intermediaries (IMC) using statutory exchange declarations (Forms 1, 2, and 5). Capital-account operations (inbound FDI, cross-border loans, portfolio investment) are also convertible but require prior or simultaneous registration with Banco de la República (Form 3 for international investment) and channeling through an IMC. Profit and dividend remittances to non-resident shareholders are permitted without a remittance license once the foreign investment is duly registered; the only operational hurdles are declaration of the operation through the IMC, availability of distributable reserves, and settlement of the applicable dividend withholding tax.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Colombia does not impose a percentage-based compulsory conversion of export receipts into COP; instead, it mandates full 'canalización' of export proceeds. All proceeds from exports of goods (Form 1) must be collected, repatriated, and channeled through an IMC within 18 months counted from the date of shipment (term extendable upon Banco de la República authorization). Once channeled, the exporter may sell the hard currency for COP at the prevailing TRM (Representative Market Rate), or deposit it in a foreign-currency account held at the IMC or in a 'cuenta de compensación' abroad previously authorized by Banco de la República and subject to periodic reporting. Retaining export proceeds offshore without such authorization constitutes a foreign exchange violation sanctionable by the SFC and may affect the deductibility of related expenses for Colombian tax purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow / Operational Checking (Cuenta Corriente) / Foreign-Currency Compensation Account / Trade Finance
Capital Escrow / Operational Checking / Foreign-Currency Compensation Account / Trade Finance
Capital Escrow / Operational Checking / Foreign-Currency Compensation Account / Trade Finance
Operational Checking (predominantly COP) / Foreign-Currency Compensation Account
Operational Checking / SWIFT settlement / Trade Finance

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for core treasury and FX functions. Colombian digital financial institutions (SEDPEs such as Nequi, Lulo and Dale wallets) are licensed for deposits and electronic payments but are not authorized IMCs and therefore cannot execute the mandatory FX channeling declarations required for trade flows. Offshore EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, Revolut Business) cannot lawfully process Colombian export proceeds or import payments subject to Forms 2/5 declarations and expose the S.A.S. to SFC/DIAN sanctions. Acceptable use is limited to minor non-FX operating expenses; all regulated agri-commodity settlement flows must remain within IMC-maintained accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical or supervised virtual interview at the onboarding branch is mandatory. Colombian tier-1 banks require the legal representative or a locally domiciled attorney-in-fact holding an apostilled, notarized power of attorney to appear in person for initial KYC; fully remote opening is generally not available for non-resident-owned commodity brokerage entities. The S.A.S. must appoint a Colombian resident authorized signatory or service agent for process of service, present apostilled constitutional documents and a valid Cámara de Comercio certificate, and submit to enhanced customer due diligence on all ultimate beneficial owners and principal traders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) opacity with non-resident shareholders holding indirect control of the S.A.S.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal (Cámara de Comercio), apostilled constitutive documents of the S.A.S. and each intermediate shareholder entity, notarized UBO declaration per SFC Circular Básica Jurídica Part 1, Title 1, Chapter 4, and a complete shareholding/control chain diagram down to the final individuals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High absolute-value, high-frequency wire activity with rapid round-trip flows typical of the brokerage model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed brokerage agreements with commission schedules, physical commodity purchase/sale contracts, commercial invoices and pro-forma invoices, bills of lading and warehouse receipts, an expected-flow matrix (counterparties, corridors, currencies, tenors), and a back-to-back settlement diagram evidencing that the S.A.S. acts as intermediary on margin rather than as principal on inventory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and embargo exposure in bulk agricultural trade (OFAC, UN, EU, CMU-Colombia Consolidated Lists) across counterparties, vessels, and ports
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening logs covering all UBOs, board members, counterparties, vessel names and IMO numbers, and load/discharge ports; OFAC and consolidated UN/EU screening evidence; compliance warranties and sanctions representation clauses embedded in the sale and brokerage contracts; and a written embargo risk policy approved by the board.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between declared business volumes and banking-flow evidence (high gross commodity flows versus thin brokerage commissions)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of RUT (Registro Único Tributario), municipal ICA tax filings, VAT returns, audited or reviewed financial statements, corporate income tax returns, and a reconciliation file mapping each gross settlement flow to the corresponding commission income line to demonstrate economic substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Split-payment and third-party settlement structures (payables directed to multiple beneficiary accounts linked to foreign principals)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written authorization letters from the foreign principal addressed to the bank, contractual provisions in the brokerage agreement supporting the split-payment instruction, KYC/KYB documentation of each ultimate beneficiary, and a legal basis memo prepared by Colombian counsel.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident investor wires equity capital via SWIFT in USD or EUR to the Colombian IMC in favor of the S.A.S. temporary capital collection account; wire instructions must identify the foreign investing entity and the purpose code (e.g., 'Aporte de capital - Inversión directa internacional'). The IMC contemporaneously files the exchange declaration Form 3 (Declaración de Cambio por Inversiones Internacionales) registering the investment with Banco de la República. The resulting certificado de cambio de inversión evidences lawful channeling and serves as the documentary basis for future dividend remittances and capital repatriation without further central bank authorization.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements are cleared through the IMC using: (i) SWIFT MT103 direct transfers for commission payments, advances, and smaller trade payments, declared under Form 5 (services) or Form 2 (goods) as appropriate; and (ii) irrevocable, transferable commercial letters of credit (UCP 600) issued by the Colombian IMC in favor of the offshore seller, which is the preferred rail for high-value bulk grain parcels because the documentary package (invoice, bill of lading, inspection, weight certificates) simultaneously satisfies the FX declaration requirement and mitigates settlement and counterparty risk. MT202 cover payments and acceptances support LC confirmations or negotiations by correspondent banks. Every disbursement must be matched against the underlying commercial invoice and transport documents to ensure the declared purpose code is accurate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/COP outright forwards (deliverable, OTC, contracted with a licensed IMC)
USD/COP non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referenced to the Colombian TRM
Cross-currency swaps (COP/USD) OTC with authorized bank counterparties for term-matched hedging
Plain-vanilla OTC FX options (calls and puts on USD/COP) covering trade receivables and payables
Rolling FX forward portfolios limited to documented underlying commodity trade exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil (Annual Commercial Registration Renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social de la sociedad
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each calendar year, from the first business day of January through March 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers a 100% surcharge on the standard tariff. Failure to renew for five consecutive years results in administrative strike-off and cancellation of the mercantile registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Estados Financieros Anuales (Annual Financial Statements Filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual shareholder assembly must approve the year-end financial statements no later than March 31; filing with the Chamber of Commerce must occur within 30 days after approval (typically by April 30).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file in the statutory term may block the annual renewal process and subject the company to regulatory fines of up to 100 SMLMV imposed by the Superintendencia de Sociedades.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración Anual de Beneficiarios Finales (Annual UBO/UBO Confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales – RUBF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, on the same deadline as the corporate income tax return, typically between April 9 and April 23 depending on the NIT last digit.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or inaccurate filing is subject to fines under Article 651 of the Tax Code of up to 1,000 UVT per violation and may affect the issuance of compliance certificates.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A S.A.S. is required to appoint a Revisor Fiscal (statutory auditor) when, as of the prior fiscal year-end, total gross assets exceed 5,000 SMLMV, or total gross annual income exceeds 5,000 SMLMV, or the company has more than 20 shareholders, or it is a controlling or controlled entity of a business group.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Full IFRS as adopted in Colombia (NIIF Plenas) issued by the CTCP, regulated by Decreto 2420 de 2015 and subsequent amendments.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, the S.A.S. must review and confirm its final beneficiary information. The annual confirmation is submitted to DIAN along with the corporate income tax return. Any transfer of 10% or more of issued shares or voting rights must be reported to DIAN within 15 calendar days of the transfer and reflected in the Chamber of Commerce renewal application.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% (general rate applicable to legal entities for taxable years 2024 onwards under Article 240 of the Tax Code; no sectoral surtax applies to a grain wholesaler under ISIC 4631 – NAICS 424510)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday exists for a Colombian S.A.S. engaged in agri-commodity trading. Effective reductions arise only through (i) the foreign-tax credit and double-taxation relief for taxes paid abroad on foreign-source income (Article 254 E.T.), (ii) the optional reinvestment/technology-deduction regimes available under the SIMPLE plan for small taxpayers (gross income ≤ 100,000 UVT ≈ COP 4,706,000,000 for 2024), and (iii) the unlimited deductibility of costs directly linked to export trading operations, including ICC arbitration, demurrage, freight, and documentary credit fees. Dividend distributions are taxed only at the shareholder level and are not deductible at the corporate level.
